title: Real frames. Incomplete story.
summary: Inspect the edit before judging its meaning.
narration: A video can contain authentic frames and still leave out part of the story. Someone can remove context or rearrange events without generating a single frame. CONTEXT traces an edit to its source, so we can inspect the evidence before deciding what it means.

title: One edit. A source collection.
summary: Local search. Cached fingerprints. Ambiguity stays visible.
narration: Start with a collection of original recordings. CONTEXT indexes each source once, then compares an uploaded edit against those visual sequences. Here, the search selects the matching recording and opens its evidence timeline. This is local collection search, not internet-wide discovery. When similar recordings compete, the result stays unresolved.

title: Follow every supported match.
summary: Blue: matched footage. Copper: supported omission. Gray: unresolved.
narration: The published clip and original run on separate, linked timelines. Blue spans show supported visual matches. Copper marks source material outside the edit. This example removes six seconds from a licensed film excerpt. It is a controlled demonstration, not a claim of discovering real misinformation. Notice that unresolved frames remain gray instead of becoming invented omissions.

title: Watch what was left out.
summary: Actual source footage. Real timestamps. Normal playback speed.
narration: Click the highlighted omission. The source player jumps to the missing interval and plays the actual footage, while the published version stays available for comparison. In this example, the edit skips part of the rabbit emerging and stretching. We can inspect that difference directly. Whether an edit changes meaning remains a separate question.

title: Read context. Inspect claims.
summary: Saved real Muse Spark response. No fresh inference is implied.
narration: Muse Spark reviews two bounded excerpts: source context and the published sequence around the cut. Available audio is retained. Here we open a saved response from a real Meta API request. The model separates observations, possible effects on interpretation, and uncertainty. Every observation must cite a supplied clip and an in-range timestamp. The server rejects invalid citations, rather than presenting them as evidence.

title: A citation returns to the footage.
summary: Timestamp bounds checked. Model claims still need scrutiny.
narration: Click a citation to return to the original or published footage at the referenced time. The interface shows exactly which excerpts were reviewed and whether they contained audio. Citation bounds are checked, but a valid timestamp does not prove that the model's interpretation is correct. That limitation stays visible.

title: A case you can reopen.
summary: Media hashes. Method. Intervals. Saved interpretation.
narration: Download the measured evidence report, including source hashes, intervals, analysis method, and limitations. Reload the case, and the investigation returns with its valid saved review. Cache reuse is tied to the exact media, finding, method, and model, so an old interpretation cannot silently attach to different evidence.

title: See the whole story.
summary: 51 backend tests. 8 browser tests. Measured limits.
narration: Controlled tests exposed and fixed false omissions and unsupported speed mappings. The current build passes fifty-one backend and eight browser tests. CONTEXT helps people examine what changed, and what remains uncertain. See the whole story.
